## Context / Problem

rebar's gates verify that a plan is grounded and self-consistent; none asks whether the
system is SIMPLER afterward. The mechanism ratchet
(`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py`) censuses seven mechanism kinds and blocks an
unjustified addition, but a `new` key passes on nothing more than a nonblank in-tree
marker (`scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:89-92`), and `parse_marker`
(`scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:37-44`) yields kind, name and reason. Nothing
parses a RETIREMENT, and nothing ever revisits a marker once admitted. The ratchet's own
docstring records the motive: 56% of sampled fixes added a mechanism against 30% that
were pure logic fixes.

Plan review does not close the gap. `A1` is the only complexity criterion and is
advisory, at `"block_threshold": 0.95` / `"default_posture": "advisory"`
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json:814-815`).

This epic makes the gates and the janitor push back on complexity GROWTH, rather than
only on complexity that is ungrounded. It was captured 2026-09-07 as an idea from the
complexity-reduction session (session log `59a7-cb88-f2f9-4148`) and authorized at full
scope by the operator on 2026-11-02.

## Measured facts, re-measured at `origin/main` `b2dca9bf5ea`

The idea's 2026-09-07 evidence has drifted. Re-measurement, which rescopes two children:

- **The code-review gate is far stronger than the idea recorded.** The idea states only
  `security` blocks, with `deletion-impact`, `scope-intent` and `tests` advisory. Today
  **12 of 24** criteria block in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`,
  including `tests` at 0.54 and `deletion-impact` at 0.6. Only `scope-intent` is still
  advisory. So `f86e` adds a TAXONOMY to an already-blocking `tests` criterion; it does
  not promote a posture.
- **Held-out twin modules number 6, not the 88 the idea recorded**:
  `test_attestation_parity_heldout_2e16.py`, `test_dead_values_heldout_7504.py`,
  `test_update_priority_heldout_c9c6.py`, `test_code_review_provenance_heldout_2d1c.py`,
  `test_reviewed_tree_binding_heldout_da31.py`, `test_snapshot_contract_heldout_8537.py`.
- **"Seam-guard" has no referent.** No `*_seam_clean_heldout.py` module exists anywhere
  in the tracked tree. `d278` is therefore scoped to held-out-twin merging only.
- **The duplicate-epic evidence holds exactly.** 8 closed epics share the title prefix
  "Restore headroom under the 800-LOC module-size cap", one deliverable filed 8 times.
- The janitor skill is `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/SKILL.md`.

## Why a project overlay, not packaged criteria

The triggers here are rebar's OWN seven-kind census and its own test conventions, which a
downstream consumer does not have; packaged criteria would fire on their plans. The new
criteria therefore live in `.rebar/`, the route `project.portability` already takes.

## Acceptance Criteria

Each criterion names one deliverable and is delivered by exactly one child.

- [ ] A blocking `project.net-mechanism` plan-review criterion exists in the `.rebar/`
      overlay, requiring a plan that adds a counted mechanism kind to name the mechanism
      it retires or state why no retirement is possible. Checked by: `fe94`'s structural
      tests asserting the criterion resolves, its posture is `blocking`, and its rubric
      body carries the threshold, finding-fields and non-findings sections.
- [ ] That criterion is calibrated against a committed eval corpus that demonstrates it
      fires on real additions. Checked by: `39bc`'s 8-case corpus under `.rebar/evals/`
      scoring at or above its recorded pass bar, reproducible from the committed spec.
- [ ] A ticket named as the sunset owner by a `# mechanism-ok:` marker cannot close while
      that marker is still present in the tree. Checked by: `d68f`'s
      deterministic completion-gate test closing a fixture ticket with the marker present
      and asserting refusal.
- [ ] The code-review `tests` criterion carries a taxonomy distinguishing behaviour tests
      from tests that pin refactor mechanics, re-export identity, LOC floors, import
      shape, or re-run a gate script. Checked by: `e508`'s calibration corpus
      (`R-reexport-*`/`FP-reexport-*`, `R-importshape-*`/`FP-importshape-*`,
      `R-gatererun-*`/`FP-gatererun-*`) in
      `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`, plus `e508`'s offline
      pairing test asserting each kind contributes exactly one fire case and one
      no-fire case. Amended 2026-11-04: NOT an overlay test asserting the taxonomy
      text is present in the rubric. The rubric's own Rule-5 exception classifies a
      prose-present grep whose only consumer is the LLM as the `change-detector`
      antipattern this criterion ships, so that check would violate the taxonomy it
      verifies. The SUBSTANCE of this AC is unchanged and is being built by `e508`;
      only the verification method changed.
- [ ] A deletion-only tidying skill exists separately from the defect audit, whose per-run ticket cap is judged by a non-positive net-complexity budget.
      Checked by: `6b48`'s assertion that the new SKILL.md admits only deletions and
      collapses, and names its budget.
- [ ] rebar-implement's epic-close phase merges held-out twin modules back into their
      parents. Checked by: `d278`'s test driving the close phase over a fixture epic
      carrying a held-out twin and asserting the twin is merged.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0 on `origin/main` with every child landed.

## Child decomposition

- `fe94` crumbly-amphibole-smelts — the net-mechanism criterion. Root; no dependencies.
- `39bc` lilac-energetic-grosbeak — its 8-case calibration corpus. Depends on `fe94`.
- `d68f` healthful-childlike-aruanas — mechanism sunset enforcement. Depends on `fe94`.
- `f86e` unwhite-worrying-bluebottle — the code-review test taxonomy. Independent.
- `6b48` reservable-honeysweet-chrysalis — the janitor split. Depends on `fe94`.
- `d278` diseased-head-vervet — held-out twin merging in the close phase. Independent,
  and narrowed by the seam-guard measurement above.

## Portability and provider neutrality

Every deliverable is a rubric, an overlay entry, a skill document, or an in-process gate
check. None reads a CI environment, so each behaves identically with no CI provider
configured. The `ci_gate` mechanism kind concerns what a PLAN says it will add, which is
recognised from prose. No deliverable names a vendor or needs a model-specific
capability, and the new rubrics are `exec: 1-TURN`.
